learn.title: Learn ISL
learn.subtitle: The fingerspelling alphabet and tips for signing well.

alphabet.title: Alphabet
alphabet.description: Every letter of the fingerspelling alphabet as a hand diagram. Tap a letter to see it move, or to record it.
alphabet.sourceNotice: Letter diagrams are recordings made on this phone. The app does not ship verified ISL alphabet images yet, so ask a fluent ISL signer or teacher to record or check them.

learn.tipsIntro: Good practice when you communicate in sign language.
learn.tipsReview: General guidance about communicating with Deaf people. Review by ISL educators is pending.

attention.title: Get attention the right way
attention.body: Wave your hand where the person can see it, or tap them lightly on the shoulder. Don't grab their hands or shout.

face.title: Face each other
face.body: Keep eye contact while signing. Sign language is visual: turning away or looking at your phone breaks the conversation.

light.title: Light your face and hands
light.body: Sit where light falls on you, not behind you. A bright window at your back makes your face and hands hard to see.

expression.title: Use your face
expression.body: Facial expressions are part of sign language grammar: they show questions, emphasis and feeling. Don't keep a blank face.

fingerspell.title: Fingerspell names clearly
fingerspell.body: Fingerspell names and words that have no sign. Keep a steady pace, hold each letter briefly, and pause between words.

language.title: ISL is its own language
language.body: Indian Sign Language has its own grammar and word order. It is not Hindi or English word by word, so don't expect a sign for every word.

regional.title: Signs vary by region
regional.body: Like spoken languages, ISL has regional variants. If someone uses a different sign, ask them to show you theirs.

check.title: Check you understood
check.body: It is fine to ask someone to repeat or to sign more slowly. Confirm important details such as numbers, dates and addresses.

space.title: Keep your signing space clear
space.body: Sign in front of your upper body, where your hands can be seen clearly. Put things in your hands down and avoid busy backgrounds.

interpreter.title: Use an interpreter when it matters
interpreter.body: For medical, legal, police or emergency situations, use a qualified ISL interpreter. This app is not a substitute.

community.title: Learn from Deaf people
community.body: The best way to learn ISL is from Deaf teachers and the Deaf community. Apps and videos are a start, not a replacement.

intro.title: How it works
intro.subtitle: Three things to know before you start.
intro.signBody: Point the camera at someone signing. Signs from the app's sign vocabulary appear as text and can be spoken aloud.
intro.textTitle: Says when it is not sure
intro.textBody: If it cannot tell what was signed, it says so instead of guessing.
intro.privacyBody: Video never leaves your phone and is never saved. Hand tracking runs on the phone.

teach.instructions: Keep your head, shoulders and hands in view. Press Record, wait for the countdown, sign once, then lower your hands.

teach.different: This take looks quite different from your earlier ones. Keep it only if you signed the same sign.
teach.problemTitle: That take could not be used

problems.no_signer: No one was in view. Stand so your head and shoulders are inside the frame.
problems.no_hands: No hands were seen. Sign in front of your body, inside the frame.

teach.saveFailed: The take could not be saved. The phone may be low on storage.
teach.doneMessage: This sign can now be recognized in Sign → Text and shown in Text → ISL. More takes make recognition more reliable.
teach.doneLetter: This letter now appears in the alphabet and can be used to fingerspell.
